NKJV.1: “Since times are not hidden from the Almighty, Why do those who know Him see not His days?
NKJV.2: “Some remove landmarks; They seize flocks violently and feed on them;
NKJV.3: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; They take the widow’s ox as a pledge.
NKJV.4: They push the needy off the road; All the poor of the land are forced to hide.
NKJV.5: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, They go out to their work, searching for food. The wilderness yields food for them and for their children.
NKJV.6: They gather their fodder in the field And glean in the vineyard of the wicked.
NKJV.7: They spend the night naked, without clothing, And have no covering in the cold.
NKJV.8: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, And huddle around the rock for want of shelter.
NKJV.9: “Some snatch the fatherless from the breast, And take a pledge from the poor.
NKJV.10: They cause the poor to go naked, without clothing; And they take away the sheaves from the hungry.
NKJV.11: They press out oil within their walls, And tread winepresses, yet suffer thirst.
NKJV.12: The dying groan in the city, And the souls of the wounded cry out; Yet God does not charge them with wrong.
NKJV.13: “There are those who rebel against the light; They do not know its ways Nor abide in its paths.
NKJV.14: The murderer rises with the light; He kills the poor and needy; And in the night he is like a thief.
NKJV.15: The eye of the adulterer waits for the twilight, Saying, ‘No eye will see me’; And he disguises his face.
NKJV.16: In the dark they break into houses Which they marked for themselves in the daytime;  They do not know the light.
NKJV.17: For the morning is the same to them as the shadow of death; If someone recognizes them, They are in the terrors of the shadow of death.
NKJV.18: “They should be swift on the face of the waters, Their portion should be cursed in the earth, So that no one would turn into the way of their vineyards.
NKJV.19: As drought and heat consume the snow waters, So the grave consumes those who have sinned.
NKJV.20: The womb should forget him, The worm should feed sweetly on him; He should be remembered no more, And wickedness should be broken like a tree.
NKJV.21: For he preys on the barren who do not bear, And does no good for the widow.
NKJV.22: “But God draws the mighty away with His power; He rises up, but no man is sure of life.
NKJV.23: He gives them security, and they rely on it; Yet His eyes are on their ways.
NKJV.24: They are exalted for a little while, Then they are gone. They are brought low; They are taken out of the way like all others; They dry out like the heads of grain.
NKJV.25: “Now if it is not so, who will prove me a liar, And make my speech worth nothing?”

ESV.1: “Why are not times of judgment kept by the Almighty, and why do those who know him never see his days?
ESV.2: Some move landmarks; they seize flocks and pasture them.
ESV.3: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; they take the widow's ox for a pledge.
ESV.4: They thrust the poor off the road; the poor of the earth all hide themselves.
ESV.5: Behold, like wild donkeys in the desert the poor  go out to their toil, seeking game; the wasteland yields food for their children.
ESV.6: They gather their  fodder in the field, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked man.
ESV.7: They lie all night naked, without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.
ESV.8: They are wet with the rain of the mountains and cling to the rock for lack of shelter.
ESV.9: (There are those who snatch the fatherless child from the breast, and they take a pledge against the poor.)
ESV.10: They go about naked, without clothing; hungry, they carry the sheaves;
ESV.11: among the olive rows of the wicked  they make oil; they tread the winepresses, but suffer thirst.
ESV.12: From out of the city the dying  groan, and the soul of the wounded cries for help; yet God charges no one with wrong.
ESV.13: “There are those who rebel against the light, who are not acquainted with its ways, and do not stay in its paths.
ESV.14: The murderer rises before it is light, that he may kill the poor and needy, and in the night he is like a thief.
ESV.15: The eye of the adulterer also waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me’; and he veils his face.
ESV.16: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves up; they do not know the light.
ESV.17: For deep darkness is morning to all of them; for they are friends with the terrors of deep darkness.
ESV.18: “You say, ‘Swift are they on the face of the waters; their portion is cursed in the land; no treader turns toward their vineyards.
ESV.19: Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters; so does Sheol those who have sinned.
ESV.20: The womb forgets them; the worm finds them sweet; they are no longer remembered, so wickedness is broken like a tree.’
ESV.21: “They wrong the barren, childless woman, and do no good to the widow.
ESV.22: Yet God  prolongs the life of the mighty by his power; they rise up when they despair of life.
ESV.23: He gives them security, and they are supported, and his eyes are upon their ways.
ESV.24: They are exalted a little while, and then are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like the heads of grain.
ESV.25: If it is not so, who will prove me a liar and show that there is nothing in what I say?”

NASB.1: 'Why are times not stored up by the Almighty, And why do those who know Him not see His days?
NASB.2: 'Some remove the landmarks; They seize and devour flocks.
NASB.3: 'They drive away the donkeys of the orphans; They take the widow's ox for a pledge.
NASB.4: 'They push the needy aside from the road; The poor of the land are made to hide themselves altogether.
NASB.5: 'Behold, as wild donkeys in the wilderness They go forth seeking food in their activity, As bread for [their] children in the desert.
NASB.6: 'They harvest their fodder in the field And glean the vineyard of the wicked.
NASB.7: 'They spend the night naked, without clothing, And have no covering against the cold.
NASB.8: 'They are wet with the mountain rains And hug the rock for want of a shelter.
NASB.9: 'Others snatch the orphan from the breast, And against the poor they take a pledge.
NASB.10: 'They cause [the poor] to go about naked without clothing, And they take away the sheaves from the hungry.
NASB.11: 'Within the walls they produce oil; They tread wine presses but thirst.
NASB.12: 'From the city men groan, And the souls of the wounded cry out; Yet God does not pay attention to folly.
NASB.13: 'Others have been with those who rebel against the light; They do not want to know its ways Nor abide in its paths.
NASB.14: 'The murderer arises at dawn; He kills the poor and the needy, And at night he is as a thief.
NASB.15: 'The eye of the adulterer waits for the twilight, Saying, 'No eye will see me.' And he disguises his face.
NASB.16: 'In the dark they dig into houses, They shut themselves up by day; They do not know the light.
NASB.17: 'For the morning is the same to him as thick darkness, For he is familiar with the terrors of thick darkness.
NASB.18: 'They are insignificant on the surface of the water; Their portion is cursed on the earth. They do not turn toward the vineyards.
NASB.19: 'Drought and heat consume the snow waters, [So does] Sheol [those who] have sinned.
NASB.20: 'A mother will forget him; The worm feeds sweetly till he is no longer remembered. And wickedness will be broken like a tree.
NASB.21: 'He wrongs the barren woman And does no good for the widow.
NASB.22: 'But He drags off the valiant by His power; He rises, but no one has assurance of life.
NASB.23: 'He provides them with security, and they are supported; And His eyes are on their ways.
NASB.24: 'They are exalted a little while, then they are gone; Moreover, they are brought low and like everything gathered up; Even like the heads of grain they are cut off.
NASB.25: 'Now if it is not so, who can prove me a liar, And make my speech worthless?'

NLT.1:
“Why doesn’t the Almighty bring the wicked to judgment?
Why must the godly wait for him in vain?
NLT.2:
Evil people steal land by moving the boundary markers.
They steal livestock and put them in their own pastures.
NLT.3:
They take the orphan’s donkey
and demand the widow’s ox as security for a loan.
NLT.4:
The poor are pushed off the path;
the needy must hide together for safety.
NLT.5:
Like wild donkeys in the wilderness,
the poor must spend all their time looking for food,
searching even in the desert for food for their children.
NLT.6:
They harvest a field they do not own,
and they glean in the vineyards of the wicked.
NLT.7:
All night they lie naked in the cold,
without clothing or covering.
NLT.8:
They are soaked by mountain showers,
and they huddle against the rocks for want of a home.
NLT.9:
“The wicked snatch a widow’s child from her breast,
taking the baby as security for a loan.
NLT.10:
The poor must go about naked, without any clothing.
They harvest food for others while they themselves are starving.
NLT.11:
They press out olive oil without being allowed to taste it,
and they tread in the winepress as they suffer from thirst.
NLT.12:
The groans of the dying rise from the city,
and the wounded cry for help,
yet God ignores their moaning.
NLT.13:
“Wicked people rebel against the light.
They refuse to acknowledge its ways
or stay in its paths.
NLT.14:
The murderer rises in the early dawn
to kill the poor and needy;
at night he is a thief.
NLT.15:
The adulterer waits for the twilight,
saying, ‘No one will see me then.’
He hides his face so no one will know him.
NLT.16:
Thieves break into houses at night
and sleep in the daytime.
They are not acquainted with the light.
NLT.17:
The black night is their morning.
They ally themselves with the terrors of the darkness.
NLT.18:
“But they disappear like foam down a river.
Everything they own is cursed,
and they are afraid to enter their own vineyards.
NLT.19:
The grave consumes sinners
just as drought and heat consume snow.
NLT.20:
Their own mothers will forget them.
Maggots will find them sweet to eat.
No one will remember them.
Wicked people are broken like a tree in the storm.
NLT.21:
They cheat the woman who has no son to help her.
They refuse to help the needy widow.
NLT.22:
“God, in his power, drags away the rich.
They may rise high, but they have no assurance of life.
NLT.23:
They may be allowed to live in security,
but God is always watching them.
NLT.24:
And though they are great now,
in a moment they will be gone like all others,
cut off like heads of grain.
NLT.25:
Can anyone claim otherwise?
Who can prove me wrong?”

AMP.1:
"Why does the Almighty not set seasons for judgment?
Why do those who know Him not see His days [for punishment of the wicked]?
AMP.2:
"Some remove the landmarks;
They [violently] seize and pasture flocks [appropriating land and flocks openly].
AMP.3:
"They drive away the donkeys of the orphans;
They take the widow's ox for a pledge.
AMP.4:
"They crowd the needy off the road;
The poor of the land all hide themselves.
AMP.5:
"Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert,
The poor go to their work, diligently seeking food;
As bread for their children in the desert.
AMP.6:
"They harvest their fodder in a field [that is not their own],
And glean the vineyard of the wicked.
AMP.7:
"They spend the night naked, without clothing,
And have no covering against the cold.
AMP.8:
"They are wet from the rain of the mountains
And cling to the rock for lack of shelter.
AMP.9:
"Others snatch the fatherless [infants] from the breast [to sell or make them slaves],
And against the poor they take a pledge [of clothing].
AMP.10:
"They cause the poor to go about naked without clothing,
And they take away the sheaves [of grain] from the hungry.
AMP.11:
"Within the walls [of the wicked] the poor make [olive] oil;
They tread [the grapes in] the wine presses, but thirst.
AMP.12:
"From the [populous and crowded] city men groan,
And the souls of the wounded cry out for help;
Yet God [seemingly] does not pay attention to the wrong [done to them].
AMP.13:
"Others have been with those who rebel against the light;
They do not want to know its ways
Nor stay in its paths.
AMP.14:
"The murderer rises at dawn;
He kills the poor and the needy,
And at night he becomes a thief.
AMP.15:
"The eye of the adulterer waits for the twilight,
Saying, 'No eye will see me,'
And he covers his face.
AMP.16:
"In the dark they dig into [the penetrable walls of] houses;
They shut themselves up by day;
They do not know the light [of day].
AMP.17:
"For the morning is the same to him as the thick darkness [of midnight];
For he is familiar with the terrors of thick darkness.
AMP.18:
"They are insignificant on the surface of the water;
Their portion is cursed on the earth;
They do not turn toward the vineyards.
AMP.19:
"Drought and heat consume the snow waters;
So does Sheol (the nether world, the place of the dead) [consume] those who have sinned.
AMP.20:
"A mother will forget him;
The worm feeds on him until he is no longer remembered.
And wickedness will be broken like a tree [which cannot be restored].
AMP.21:
"He preys on the barren (childless) woman
And does no good for the widow.
AMP.22:
"Yet God draws away the mighty by His power;
He rises, but no one has assurance of life.
AMP.23:
"God gives them security, and they are supported;
And His eyes are on their ways.
AMP.24:
"They are exalted for a little while, and then they are gone;
Moreover, they are brought low and like everything [they are] gathered up and taken out of the way;
Even like the heads of grain they are cut off.
AMP.25:
"And if this is not so, who can prove me a liar
And make my speech worthless?"

The poor, like stray dogs and cats,
scavenge for food in back alleys.
MSG.6:
They sort through the garbage of the rich,
eke out survival on handouts.
MSG.7:
Homeless, they shiver through cold nights on the street;
they've no place to lay their heads.
MSG.8:
Exposed to the weather, wet and frozen,
they huddle in makeshift shelters.
MSG.9:
Nursing mothers have their babies snatched from them;
the infants of the poor are kidnapped and sold.
MSG.10:
They go about patched and threadbare;
even the hard workers go hungry.
MSG.11:
No matter how back-breaking their labor,
they can never make ends meet.
MSG.12:
People are dying right and left, groaning in torment.
The wretched cry out for help
and God does nothing, acts like nothing's wrong!
MSG.13:
"Then there are those who avoid light at all costs,
who scorn the light-filled path.
MSG.14:
When the sun goes down, the murderer gets up—
kills the poor and robs the defenseless.
MSG.15:
Sexual predators can't wait for nightfall,
thinking, 'No one can see us now.'
MSG.16:
Burglars do their work at night,
but keep well out of sight through the day.
They want nothing to do with light.
MSG.17:
Deep darkness is morning for that bunch;
they make the terrors of darkness their companions in crime.
MSG.18:
"They are scraps of wood floating on the water—
useless, cursed junk, good for nothing.
MSG.19:
As surely as snow melts under the hot, summer sun,
sinners disappear in the grave.
MSG.20:
The womb has forgotten them, worms have relished them—
nothing that is evil lasts.
MSG.21:
Unscrupulous,
they prey on those less fortunate.
MSG.22:
However much they strut and flex their muscles,
there's nothing to them. They're hollow.
MSG.23:
They may have an illusion of security,
but God has his eye on them.
MSG.24:
They may get their brief successes,
but then it's over, nothing to show for it.
Like yesterday's newspaper,
they're used to wrap up the garbage.
MSG.25:
You're free to try to prove me a liar,
but you won't be able to do it."

NRSVCE.1:
“Why are times not kept by the Almighty,
and why do those who know him never see his days?
NRSVCE.2:
The wicked remove landmarks;
they seize flocks and pasture them.
NRSVCE.3:
They drive away the donkey of the orphan;
they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
NRSVCE.4:
They thrust the needy off the road;
the poor of the earth all hide themselves.
NRSVCE.5:
Like wild asses in the desert
they go out to their toil,
scavenging in the wasteland
food for their young.
NRSVCE.6:
They reap in a field not their own
and they glean in the vineyard of the wicked.
NRSVCE.7:
They lie all night naked, without clothing,
and have no covering in the cold.
NRSVCE.8:
They are wet with the rain of the mountains,
and cling to the rock for want of shelter.
NRSVCE.9:
“There are those who snatch the orphan child from the breast,
and take as a pledge the infant of the poor.
NRSVCE.10:
They go about naked, without clothing;
though hungry, they carry the sheaves;
NRSVCE.11:
between their terraces they press out oil;
they tread the wine presses, but suffer thirst.
NRSVCE.12:
From the city the dying groan,
and the throat of the wounded cries for help;
yet God pays no attention to their prayer.
NRSVCE.13:
“There are those who rebel against the light,
who are not acquainted with its ways,
and do not stay in its paths.
NRSVCE.14:
The murderer rises at dusk
to kill the poor and needy,
and in the night is like a thief.
NRSVCE.15:
The eye of the adulterer also waits for the twilight,
saying, ‘No eye will see me’;
and he disguises his face.
NRSVCE.16:
In the dark they dig through houses;
by day they shut themselves up;
they do not know the light.
NRSVCE.17:
For deep darkness is morning to all of them;
for they are friends with the terrors of deep darkness.
NRSVCE.18:
“Swift are they on the face of the waters;
their portion in the land is cursed;
no treader turns toward their vineyards.
NRSVCE.19:
Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters;
so does Sheol those who have sinned.
NRSVCE.20:
The womb forgets them;
the worm finds them sweet;
they are no longer remembered;
so wickedness is broken like a tree.
NRSVCE.21:
“They harm the childless woman,
and do no good to the widow.
NRSVCE.22:
Yet God prolongs the life of the mighty by his power;
they rise up when they despair of life.
NRSVCE.23:
He gives them security, and they are supported;
his eyes are upon their ways.
NRSVCE.24:
They are exalted a little while, and then are gone;
they wither and fade like the mallow;
they are cut off like the heads of grain.
NRSVCE.25:
If it is not so, who will prove me a liar,
and show that there is nothing in what I say?”

NIV.1:
“Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment?
Why must those who know him look in vain for such days?
NIV.2:
Men move boundary stones;
they pasture flocks they have stolen.
NIV.3:
They drive away the orphan’s donkey
and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
NIV.4:
They thrust the needy from the path
and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
NIV.5:
Like wild donkeys in the desert,
the poor go about their labor of foraging food;
the wasteland provides food for their children.
NIV.6:
They gather fodder in the fields
and glean in the vineyards of the wicked.
NIV.7:
Lacking clothes, they spend the night naked;
they have nothing to cover themselves in the cold.
NIV.8:
They are drenched by mountain rains
and hug the rocks for lack of shelter.
NIV.9:
The fatherless child is snatched from the breast;
the infant of the poor is seized for a debt.
NIV.10:
Lacking clothes, they go about naked;
they carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
NIV.11:
They crush olives among the terraces;
they tread the winepresses, yet suffer thirst.
NIV.12:
The groans of the dying rise from the city,
and the souls of the wounded cry out for help.
But God charges no one with wrongdoing.
NIV.13:
“There are those who rebel against the light,
who do not know its ways
or stay in its paths.
NIV.14:
When daylight is gone, the murderer rises up
and kills the poor and needy;
in the night he steals forth like a thief.
NIV.15:
The eye of the adulterer watches for dusk;
he thinks, ‘No eye will see me,’
and he keeps his face concealed.
NIV.16:
In the dark, men break into houses,
but by day they shut themselves in;
they want nothing to do with the light.
NIV.17:
For all of them, deep darkness is their morning;
they make friends with the terrors of darkness.
NIV.18:
“Yet they are foam on the surface of the water;
their portion of the land is cursed,
so that no one goes to the vineyards.
NIV.19:
As heat and drought snatch away the melted snow,
so the grave snatches away those who have sinned.
NIV.20:
The womb forgets them,
the worm feasts on them;
evil men are no longer remembered
but are broken like a tree.
NIV.21:
They prey on the barren and childless woman,
and to the widow show no kindness.
NIV.22:
But God drags away the mighty by his power;
though they become established, they have no assurance of life.
NIV.23:
He may let them rest in a feeling of security,
but his eyes are on their ways.
NIV.24:
For a little while they are exalted, and then they are gone;
they are brought low and gathered up like all others;
they are cut off like heads of grain.
NIV.25:
“If this is not so, who can prove me false
and reduce my words to nothing?”

NET.1: “Why are times not appointed by the Almighty? Why do those who know him not see his days?
NET.2: Men move boundary stones; they seize the flock and pasture them.
NET.3: They drive away the orphan’s donkey; they take the widow’s ox as a pledge.
NET.4: They turn the needy from the pathway, and the poor of the land hide themselves together.
NET.5: Like wild donkeys in the desert they go out to their labor, seeking diligently for food; the wasteland provides food for them and for their children.
NET.6: They reap fodder in the field, and glean in the vineyard of the wicked.
NET.7: They spend the night naked because they lack clothing; they have no covering against the cold.
NET.8: They are soaked by mountain rains and huddle in the rocks because they lack shelter.
NET.9: The fatherless child is snatched from the breast, the infant of the poor is taken as a pledge.
NET.10: They go about naked, without clothing, and go hungry while they carry the sheaves.
NET.11: They press out the olive oil between the rows of olive trees; they tread the winepresses while they are thirsty.
NET.12: From the city the dying groan, and the wounded cry out for help, but God charges no one with wrongdoing.
NET.13: There are those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways and they do not stay on its paths.
NET.14: Before daybreak the murderer rises up; he kills the poor and the needy; in the night he is like a thief.
NET.15: And the eye of the adulterer watches for the twilight, thinking, ‘No eye can see me,’ and covers his face with a mask.
NET.16: In the dark the robber breaks into houses, but by day they shut themselves in; they do not know the light.
NET.17: For all of them, the morning is to them like deep darkness; they are friends with the terrors of darkness.
NET.18: “You say, ‘He is foam on the face of the waters; their portion of the land is cursed so that no one goes to their vineyard.
NET.19: The drought as well as the heat carry away the melted snow; so the grave takes away those who have sinned.
NET.20: The womb forgets him, the worm feasts on him, no longer will he be remembered. Like a tree, wickedness will be broken down.
NET.21: He preys on the barren and childless woman, and does not treat the widow well.
NET.22: But God drags off the mighty by his power; when God rises up against him, he has no faith in his life.
NET.23: God may let them rest in a feeling of security, but he is constantly watching all their ways.
NET.24: They are exalted for a little while, and then they are gone, they are brought low like all others, and gathered in, and like a head of grain they are cut off.’
NET.25: “If this is not so, who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”
